newsitem.title: JAPAN: TEPCO urges gov't to press ahead with reactors.
newsitem.headline: TEPCO urges gov't to press ahead with reactors.

text.p: Japan's largest power firm on Thursday urged the government to press ahead with the nation's fast breeder reactor programme and other nuclear power projects despite mounting public opposition towards atomic power.
"It is imperative to use nuclear energy which remains a major longer-term energy source (for Japan)," Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) president Hiroshi Araki said.
He was speaking at a meeting between the heads of electric power utilities and Science and Technology Agency chief Riichiro Chikaoka.
A spate of recent accidents at nuclear power plants and nuclear power-related facilities has severely undermined public faith in Japan's nuclear power industry, raising grave doubts about its future.

Araki called on the government "to responsibly see through to its completion the development of sophisticated nuclear power technology such as the fast breeder reactor and the reprocessing of nuclear waste."
The TEPCO president also told Chikaoka that a pressing issue faced by the industry was how it would store spent nuclear fuel.

"The biggest hurdle (for the electric utilities industry) is the issue of storage facilities for high-level (nuclear) waste," an electric utilities association spokesman quoted Araki as telling Chikaoka at Thursday's meeting.

One of the most serious nuclear power accidents recently was an explosion in March at a nuclear fuel reprocessing plant at Tokaimura, northeast of Tokyo, which exposed 37 workers to small doses of radiation.

The facility is run by the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC), a state run firm which is also in charge of a prototype fast breeder reactor which has been closed since an accident in December 1995.
PNC carries out research in nuclear power aiming to recycle nuclear material and help resources-poor Japan achieve energy self-efficiency through nuclear power.
